source_text: Ista corporum commixtio cum calore, cum voluptate, cum semine, a Deo facta, et pro suo modo laudabilis approbatur, quae aliquando etiam amplum efficitur munus piorum. Confitearis ergo necesse est originale, quod finxeras, interisse peccatum.
pass_a_gloss: This mixing of bodies with heat, with pleasure, with seed, made by God, is approved as praiseworthy according to its own measure, which sometimes is even made a large gift of the godly. You must therefore confess that the original sin which you had invented has perished.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: This union of bodies, with warmth, with pleasure, with seed, made by God, is recognized as praiseworthy within its proper measure. Sometimes it even becomes a great gift to the godly.
You must therefore confess that the original sin you invented has vanished.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian excerpt in the intermediary document
